title: How to Make Text Larger on Your Smartphone
excerpt: An easy guide to improving readability on iPhone and Android without replacing your phone.
introduction: Small text can make an otherwise useful phone frustrating. You can usually enlarge the words and important interface elements using accessibility settings.

sections.heading: Start with display settings
paragraphs: On an iPhone, open Settings and look for Display & Brightness, then Text Size. Move the slider until the words are comfortable to read. Larger Accessibility Sizes are available under Accessibility > Display & Text Size.
On most Android phones, open Settings and search for Font size or Display size. Menu names can vary between brands and software versions.

sections.heading: Make the screen easier to see
paragraphs: If a larger font is not enough, increase display size, adjust contrast or turn on bold text where your phone supports it.
Test the result inside the apps you use most. Some apps manage their own font size, so not every screen will change equally.

sections.heading: Keep one more shortcut handy
paragraphs: Both major phone platforms include magnification features in Accessibility. These can help with tiny text that an app does not let you resize.

title: Why Towels Still Smell After Washing
excerpt: Understand common causes of musty towel smells and practical ways to prevent them.
introduction: A freshly washed towel should smell clean. When it still smells damp or musty, the issue is often moisture, washing habits or a washing machine that needs attention.

sections.heading: Moisture is often the key
paragraphs: A towel that stays damp for too long can develop an unpleasant smell. Spread towels out to dry completely instead of leaving them in a pile or a closed hamper.
After washing, move towels to the dryer or drying rack promptly. Make sure they are fully dry before folding and storing.

sections.heading: Avoid overloading the washer
paragraphs: A tightly packed load may prevent adequate cleaning and rinsing. Follow your machine's load guidance and use the amount of detergent recommended for the load and water conditions.
More detergent is not always better. Residue may remain in fabrics if detergent is used excessively or rinsing is insufficient.

sections.heading: Check your machine
paragraphs: If several loads smell musty, inspect the washer gasket, detergent drawer and filter according to the manufacturer's manual. Run the recommended cleaning cycle when appropriate.
Never mix bleach with vinegar, ammonia or other cleaning chemicals.

title: Simple Ways to Use Less Electricity at Home
excerpt: Low-effort habits that may reduce wasted electricity without sacrificing comfort.
introduction: You do not need a complete home renovation to pay closer attention to electricity use. Start with the appliances and settings you control every day.

sections.heading: Focus on heating and cooling
paragraphs: Heating and cooling frequently represent a large part of household energy consumption. Use reasonable temperature settings, close doors and windows while equipment is running, and maintain filters as the manufacturer recommends.
If your home has a programmable thermostat, set schedules that match when the house is occupied. Avoid changes that compromise health or safety during extreme weather.

sections.heading: Look at lighting and standby power
paragraphs: Replace frequently used incandescent bulbs with appropriate LED alternatives when needed. Turn off lights in empty rooms.
Some devices consume power in standby mode. A power strip may make it easier to turn off eligible equipment, but leave devices that require continuous operation connected.

sections.heading: Measure before buying new equipment
paragraphs: Review your utility bills month by month and account for weather and changes in household use. If possible, use a plug-in power monitor to identify energy-intensive devices.
A product's advertised savings are not guaranteed for your household. Compare its total cost with realistic usage before purchasing.
